cells.tense: You are at the point where a connection is being decided, and the deciding is clear.
cells.act: keep the heading when it is contested
cells.ask: Name one commitment you actually chose, then hold its heading the next time something tugs at it — one plain refusal to drift, no speech attached.
cells.core:
You're standing at the point where a connection is still a decision, not yet a fact. The direction came from felt engagement rather than argument, which is why it can take weight. When the next pull arrives, what keeps the flow is that a heading was already set — the pull doesn't get to redraw it.

So this week: pick the commitment you actually chose, and hold that heading once, when it's contested. One refusal to drift, said plainly, nothing more. You don't have to settle whether the whole thing is right. You just have to let the next push meet a direction that stayed put.

cells.tense: You will have settled how the connection turns out before it has had room to happen.
cells.act: rest in the result of the tending
cells.ask: Sit for a while this week with something you already grew well — use it, enjoy it, add nothing — and stop improving what's done.
cells.core:
The meeting has already run its course in your head, along with both endings. So the real one keeps arriving as a test it cannot pass, and you steer before you get there. The vision is real. It has just outrun what it was supposed to describe.

Something you tended carefully is already finished and good. Turn toward that. Use it, enjoy it, or sit in it — a grown thing, received rather than improved. Growth that isn't forced holds space without clutching, and tending that produced something is where that gets practiced. What careful work produced is allowed to be enjoyed before the next thing starts.

cells.tense: You were at a point where a connection could have been chosen, and you are still at that door.
cells.act: distinguish what is yours from what you borrowed
cells.ask: Write whose each pull is — yours or picked up from someone else — and act on one you marked as yours.
cells.core:
The door was there when the thing was still open and nobody had named it. That moment sits behind you, and you stay at it, so nothing gets finished. What's thin here is not feeling but sorting. The pulls arrive mixed, yours and other people's, and undivided they read as one weight, so none of them gets picked.

Don't push yourself toward anyone. Separate the strands. Before you follow a pull, two minutes with a page: whose is this. Yours gets a mark. Then one marked-yours pull, one small move, and that's the whole week. The door stops being the only place you can stand.

cells.tense: You have been reading where a connection could go, and you would say it simply formed that way.
cells.act: walk the route with someone who is lost on it
cells.ask: Walk somebody through a passage you know — the turns it takes — and stop where they can carry it alone.
cells.core:
You see where a genuine meeting could go, and it looks to you like these things assemble themselves. They don't. Your read does the work, and the account you give leaves your hand out of it.

So walk somebody through a route you actually know — the turns it takes, out loud — then stop where they can carry it alone. You once found a passage yourself, and you still know its shape; that knowledge is older and simpler than the role it grew into. Practice without forcing looks the same at a smaller size: refinement serving a person, not a performance of having it handled.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that a specific 'genuine connection is being chosen' right now — the record says the signature marks a decisive meeting, but I can't claim who or that it's currently live for this person. A reader could reasonably say 'I'm not choosing anyone; this is all hypothetical,' and the Too Little and Too Much cells would still hold because they describe a capacity for wholehearted commitment, not a named relationship. The ask survives being wrong: tending, resting in a made thing, sorting your own pulls, and showing someone the way are useful whether or not the read about connection is right. The sentence that serves me more than them is anything that sounds like I know what they are holding back — I cut that and left the mechanism as capacity, not history. One clause I kept does the same work: in Too Much, 'you can feel it in the planning' praises a method I invented for them, so I removed it and said only what's observable.
